pillar_reactions.evidence: The three-pillar presentation never happened. The rep referenced the structure once in passing while explaining what the six-month programme is — 'Trevor is like building everything from the ground up, with training, with nutrition and accountability' — and immediately said it was not applicable: 'like the six months, I don't think that's applicable to you.' The prospect asked directly what the programme actually is and how it would differ from what he already does, and never got an answer.

Named as an agenda item in the opening — 'Then we go to the nutrition part' — and never returned to. Everything on record about his eating came from his own unprompted account: whole foods, no processed food, a 9am to 6pm eating window, high protein, never tracked anything.

Never delivered. This is the pillar that would have spoken directly to his stated situation — three and a half years self-directed, never followed anyone's programme through, stuck at a plateau he cannot solve alone — and it was the one he never heard. He had explicitly opened the door: 'I feel like a little bit of coaching might be nice.'

anchors.raw: I picked up Pavel's book on kettlebells, Simple and Sinister, followed that, took it from 35 pounds to, I don't know, sometimes I can do the 90, but like 80 pounds, one-handed swings, like Turkish get-ups, the whole thing.
anchors.note: The strongest undercutting anchor in the corpus so far: a book, priced in tens of dollars, that produced a documented three-and-a-half-year result. Any argument for $6,000 has to clear that, and the rep did not attempt one — he conceded the ground and disqualified instead. Worth noting that Pavel is the same old-school Russian kettlebell lineage the rep credits with his own recovery on other calls, so the competitor here is effectively the method's own source material.

anchors.raw: Actually, I saw one of Trevor's YouTubes and it was the every minute on the minute progressive two-handed swings with 90 pounds for 30 minutes... And then I did that and that's like a gasser for me. So I do that once a week and I was like, oh, that's a good workout.
anchors.note: Second call in this batch where the prospect is already a satisfied consumer of the free version of the product. He gets a workout he rates highly, weekly, for nothing. The paid offer has to be positioned against the company's own marketing output and there is no material for doing that.

anchors.raw: I make my own routines. I've never gotten guidance or anything.
anchors.note: Owns all his own kettlebells, is not a gym member, trains five times a week without external structure. The entire value of the offer for him would be programming and progression, and the rep confirmed the format would not deliver his specific goal, so there was nothing left to sell.

unmet_demand.want: Break a multi-year plateau at 15 strict pull-ups and reach 20
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep stated on the record that the programme's training format is the wrong tool for it: 'when it's like 20-30 minutes and it's pretty explosive and intense, I don't think that's the way to build like a typical static strength of pull-ups. That's more of a calisthenics thing to do.' He then prescribed the solution himself, for free — band-assisted reps above the ceiling, then weighted pull-ups at five reps. A genuine boundary of the product, stated plainly by the rep, and the most useful product intelligence in the batch.

unmet_demand.want: Add muscle mass while already lean, strong and training five times a week
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The programme's stated guarantee is a kettlebell load increase and its positioning is fat loss as a by-product, neither of which is hypertrophy for a lean 41-year-old. Whether Trevor programmes for mass gain was neither asked nor answered. This is the same unanswered question Anthony Sosa raised on 2026-07-07 ('can I get that same anabolic stimulus from just kettlebells'), so it is a pattern rather than a one-off.

unmet_demand.want: A clear answer to 'how is it going to differ from what I'm doing now?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked the question directly at 00:08:13 and the answer he got was that the programme would be tailored to his schedule and level. For a man who already writes his own programmes off a book, tailoring is not a differentiator. Nobody described form review, progression modelling or the weekly check-in, which are the things a book cannot do.
